newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's chocolate-lovers boost cocoa imports.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's chocolate-lovers boost cocoa imports.

text.p: The Ukrainians' love of sweet things is translating into rising cocoa imports and a growing chocolate market, trade and industry sources said on Thursday.

"We imported about 4,000 tonnes of cocoa beans last year, will import 5,500 tonnes this year, and expect to import 7,000 tonnes next year," said Stanyslav Myronenko, chief executive of UkrKonditerProm, the state sweets concern.
He said business at the country's seven chocolate factories -- all privatised -- was brisk despite Ukraine's poor economic situation.
"The market is growing stronger," Myronenko said.
Cocoa butter, cocoa liquor, nuts, pepper, coffee and tea were also being imported by UkrKonditerProm, he added.

Mykola Shvetz, manager of chocolate maker Ukraina, a joint venture with Kraft Jacobs Suchard SA based in the eastern city of Sumy, said they kept the price of their Korona chocolate bar low. The big, 100 gram bar costs one hyrvnia ($1.87).
"We sell chocolate at a low price and business is very good. The general tendency is for sales to increase," Shvetz said.
Local brands have to compete with Western bars like Mars and Snickers which sell at street kiosks even in rural Ukraine. But manufacturers say their brands are holding their own.

A director at the Lviv Svitoch chocolate factory in western Ukraine, privatised in 1990, said the company expected to produce 12,000-13,000 tonnes of chocolate bars and candy this year compared to 10,000 tonnes in 1995.
"We will produce even more next year," said production superviser Maria Protz. "We plan to add a new production line."
Protz said individual sweets sold by the kilo, chocolate bars and boxed chocolates were selling equally well.
Svitoch, considered a privatisation success story, operates more than 20 stores across Ukraine.
It has helped boost sales by replacing dull Soviet packaging with individually wrapped chocolates and colourful boxes.
Protz said she expected demand to increase at Christmas and for the New Year holiday, particularly for children's sweets, Svyaty Nykolay and Snihovy Zaichyk -- St. Nick and Snow Bunny.
"Ukrainians like sweets, just like people the world over," she said. --Irene Marushko, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
